newsitem.title: PERU: Peru delays Yauliyacu transfer to Paranapanema.
newsitem.headline: Peru delays Yauliyacu transfer to Paranapanema.

text.p: Peruvian state miner Centromin said Tuesday it delayed the scheduled transfer of polymetallic unit Empresa Minera Yauliyacu to Brazil's Paranapanema.
"There were some documents missing. Probably they didn't arrive because of the carnival holiday in Brazil," said Centromin spokesman Enrique Olivares.
Paranapanema bought Yauliyacu for $12.7 million at auction last December. The formal transfer was scheduled for Tuesday.
"We are waiting for those documents for the transfer," said Olivares without specifying when that could be.

At the December auction, Paranapanema beat out bids from Pan American Silver Corp of Canada, Sunshine Mining and Refining Co of the U.S., Glencore International AG of Switzerland and Compania Minera Casapalca of Peru.
Centromin had set a minimum bid price for the unit of $8 million and a minimum investment of $15 million over five years. The Brazilian mining company offered to invest $100 million over five years.
According to Centromin, the unit has proven and probable reserves of silver, zinc, lead and copper totalling 7.3 million tonnes. The unit's potential reserves total 14.7 million tonnes.
In 1995, 746,000 tonnes of mineral were extracted from the site.
The auction was part of Centromin's privatization.
